## Who shares our characteristics
STXBP1 sits in the Neurotransmitter release cycle group. [8b8a74101835d1d2]
STX1B disease shows a shared research pattern with STXBP1. [ab5fe5ff268d13ba]
VAMP2 disease shows a shared research pattern with STXBP1. [ca33d6f8f475990e]
SNAP25 disease shows a shared research pattern with STXBP1. [fcb938d1b0386f7c]

## What already exists
A natural history study for STXBP1 is listed. [bc71e274e1c691ec]
A joint natural history study for STXBP1 and SYNGAP1 is listed. [dcec503694916ae3, 4c2106f026e81f1e]
The joint study covers about 12 percent of DNM1 features, 6 of 39 terms. [dcec503694916ae3, 038039c482e85db7, 041c3c175e2cb26b, 049ef546da3cdfdc, 6df8a36e97901f12]
Asociación Síndrome STXBP1 in Spain serves this disease. [453d4be996145f4e]
The European STXBP1 Consortium has a patient registry. [ba44da54694ec39f]
Raging Raymond Foundation focuses on VAMP2 syndrome. [202ca5201eca2102]

## What differs and must be verified
GNAO1 disease can look similar but shows no shared mechanism here, so we exclude it. [f94ad5494a3e9ab8]
CACNA1A disease overlaps only weakly in insulin secretion, a different step. [34c9bc447921f8cb, 3a40a3f53a18b664, 187be2699f417de6]
SLC2A1 disease overlaps only weakly in insulin secretion, a different step. [20c30f77dc2491fb, 3a40a3f53a18b664, 5490966f0991bdf8]
GRIN1 disease overlaps only weakly in neurexins and neuroligins, a different step. [9b5a310872598764, 072a91fd2fdb335f, ce6dd3aad07a277e]
DNM1 disease overlaps only weakly in vesicle organization, a different step. [6df8a36e97901f12, 34c673fba26b1793, f1a54e7fce5ac22f]
STXBP1 shows loss of function evidence; CACNA1A shows gain of function evidence. [87257c69fcfbcdad, df57b34e24ef5206, 4e69b8ecbf6740e9, c3ec464ea6412040]
STXBP1 shows loss of function evidence; GRIN1 shows gain of function evidence. [87257c69fcfbcdad, df57b34e24ef5206, c9e703902a0fb3f5, 0211d2b50f1f9730]
Findings conflict inside STXBP1: no link between seizure severity and disability severity. [b1f9e5eeafbc81d2]
Findings conflict inside STXBP1: no clear link between mutation type and seizures or outcomes. [e362983ef11a54b1]
Findings conflict inside STXBP1: recurrent variants do not match distinct syndromes. [ddc8cd6784a496fb]

## Who to contact
Ingo Helbig has published on both STXBP1 and DNM1. [1787b8db0c61e674, 18e9e45f700b90dd]
Sarah McKeown Ruggiero has published on both STXBP1 and DNM1. [3e4ae99a27cf8209, 54fc3ff5f2a9b51f]
Katherine L Helbig has published on both STXBP1 and DNM1. [270b287e0a68cd44, 4a0508e26e9d06db]

## Proposed first joint step
Review STXBP1 and SYNGAP1 Related Disorders Natural History Study (NCT06555965) eligibility for DNM1-related disease and contact Ingo Helbig. [dcec503694916ae3, 038039c482e85db7, 041c3c175e2cb26b, 049ef546da3cdfdc, 6df8a36e97901f12, 0bead7fade435d02, 1787b8db0c61e674, 18e9e45f700b90dd]

## Search coverage
Coverage of DNM1-related disease (developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 31B) phenotype information is 12% (6 of 39 terms; IC 20.63/167.43) using STXBP1 and SYNGAP1 Related Disorders Natural History Study. [dcec503694916ae3, 038039c482e85db7, 041c3c175e2cb26b]
